correctness.rationale: The two-sorted incidence xIy iff HammingDist(x,y)<=1 gives closed intents as intersections of full radius-one balls B_x. For distinct centers, pair intersections are coordinate lines if distance1, two intermediate points if distance2, and empty otherwise. All singletons are triple intersections for d>=2; atoms are singletons and coatoms the distinct maximal balls, so lattice order automorphisms correspond exactly to attribute permutations preserving the ball family. For q>=3, coordinate lines (size q, except already recognizable coatoms) are invariant, and their collinearity recovers H(d,q), whose graph automorphism group is S_q wr S_d. For q=2, embed attributes into even and objects into odd halves of F2^(d+1) with appended parity; incidence iff lifted cube adjacency, whose sort-preserving group is even translations ⋊S_(d+1). Group order 2^d(d+1)!, index d+1 over Q_d graph automorphisms. An extra-coordinate/parity swap witnesses strictness. Independent complete ball-family permutation counts (d,q)=(2,2),(3,2),(2,3) equal 24,192,72. The unbounded conclusion is the group argument, not finite counts.

originality.rationale: PASS on the specific full concept-lattice automorphism group and sharp binary-extra-coordinate symmetry, with relevant implicit two-fold graph-aut risk. Classical Hamming graph automorphisms (Mirafzal–Ziaee) account exactly for q>=3 and the natural subgroup for q=2. Rawson et al give a general concept-lattice/hyperedge intersection encoding; a published Resultary Hamming Čech theorem supplies closed-ball intersection lemmas. Neither of those mathematical statements implies the complete group classification without recovering lattice atoms, coatoms and parity graph symmetries.
